messages.content: My landlord texted me that rent goes up next week. My lease still has 4 months left.
Start by checking the lease clause on rent changes during an active term. In most cases, fixed-term leases cannot be changed unilaterally before renewal unless the contract allows it.
The lease says rent is fixed through December. There is no early-adjustment clause.
That language is strong for your position. Preserve the lease PDF, payment history, and all landlord messages in one folder with timestamps.
Can they still file eviction if I keep paying the original amount?
They can file, but whether they win depends on lease terms and local law. If your lease is fixed and you pay on time, your defense is typically stronger.
What should I send them right now?
Send a short written response: cite the lease section, state you will continue paying the contractual amount, and request confirmation that your account reflects the lease rate.
Should I mention tenant protection laws in the message?
You can mention them briefly, but keep the tone factual. Overloading the first message with legal citations can escalate conflict early.
Can you give me a clean template?

Template: 'I received your notice regarding rent increase. Per Section X of our lease, rent is fixed at $Y through DATE. I will continue paying the lease amount on schedule. Please confirm my ledger reflects this.'
I got a red-light ticket, but the signal was flashing irregularly. I have dashcam video.
Great start. Preserve the original video file, keep metadata intact, and export a copy for court submission.
I also took pictures of the intersection 30 minutes later.
Add those photos to an evidence timeline and note exact capture times. Courts care about chronology and consistency.
Should I request signal maintenance records?
Yes. If available via records request, maintenance logs can strengthen your argument that the signal condition was abnormal.
The hearing is in two weeks. What do I bring?
Bring citation copy, timeline, printed photos, video on USB, and a one-page statement summarizing facts and requested outcome.
Can I ask for reduction instead of full dismissal?
Yes, request primary relief (dismissal) and alternative relief (reduction/no points). Having a fallback can be practical.
How should I speak in court?
Use short factual statements: what happened, what evidence shows, and what ruling you request. Avoid speculation and emotional language.
I paid a contractor a $3,000 deposit and they stopped answering calls.
First, organize contract, invoice, payment proof, and communication history. Small claims outcomes often hinge on documentation quality.
I have Zelle receipts and text messages. No formal invoice.
That can still work. Build a timeline with dates, amounts, and project milestones promised versus delivered.
Do I need to send a demand letter before filing?
Usually yes, and it is strategically useful. Send a clear demand with amount due, reason, and deadline to cure.
What deadline should I give?
10 to 14 days is common for pre-suit demand letters, unless local rules specify otherwise.
Can I include filing fees and service costs?
Yes, typically you can request principal damages plus allowable court costs. Keep each category itemized.
Please draft a concise demand letter opening.

Opening: 'This letter serves as formal demand for return of $3,000 paid on DATE for contracted services not performed. If payment is not received by DATE, I will proceed with small claims filing without further notice.'
My offer letter has a non-compete and non-solicit. I am not sure what is normal.
We should evaluate duration, geography, restricted activities, and whether compensation supports the restriction.
Non-compete says 24 months across the entire US.
That is broad in many jurisdictions. Enforceability often weakens when scope exceeds legitimate business need.
Can I negotiate it before signing?
Yes. Try narrowing to 6-12 months, defined competitors, and specific role functions rather than blanket restrictions.
What about non-solicit of clients and employees?
Non-solicit clauses are often more enforceable than non-competes if tailored and time-limited.
There is also an IP assignment clause.
Check carve-outs for prior inventions and side projects. Add an exhibit listing anything you created before employment.
Can you give me a negotiation line I can send HR?
Suggested line: 'I am excited to join and would like to align restrictive covenants with my role. Could we revise non-compete scope to specific competitors and a shorter duration?'
